title: Research
text:
RESEARCH


Questions worth investigating
AI Governance Lab explores how evidence can make AI governance decisions more informed, transparent, and accountable. These are emerging research interests, not a catalogue of completed work.




AI governance and accountability
How can institutions assess claims about AI systems and translate evidence into meaningful oversight and accountability?
Real-world example: A government agency uses AI to help decide who receives public services. How can it explain those decisions, check for unfair outcomes, and remain accountable to the people affected?


AI safety and risk evaluation
What can evaluations tell us about the risks of AI systems, and which uncertainties remain when findings are applied outside controlled settings?
Real-world example: A hospital considers using an AI tool to support medical decisions. How can it test when the tool makes mistakes and whether it remains reliable with different patients?


Societal impact and public policy
How can we examine the real-world consequences of AI deployment, including who benefits, who bears costs, and under what conditions?
Real-world example: A city introduces AI to improve public transport. Does it actually help commuters, and are the benefits shared across neighborhoods?


Empirical methods
Where can statistics, causal inference, impact evaluation, and applied machine learning improve the quality of evidence used in governance?
Real-world example: After a public agency adopts AI, processing times fall. Did AI cause the improvement, or did other changes happen at the same time?



These examples are illustrative, not completed studies. Specific research questions and methods will be refined as individual projects develop.

title: Projects
text:
AI Governance Evidence Lab
A proposed framework for examining evidence behind claims about AI systems. It asks what evaluations, audits, and observations actually establish - and how governance decisions should account for uncertainty.
The concept includes an illustrative case on AI-assisted hiring.
It is not a validated assessment tool or completed empirical study.

AI Impact Self-Assessment
An early-stage concept exploring how an AI-assisted, human-in-the-loop approach could help organizations reflect on the societal impacts of their AI applications, examine supporting evidence, and identify potential risks and gaps.
It is a proposed approach, not an operational or validated assessment tool.
